observedLoci.subject: Communion shared declarations and unresolved bodily presence
Printed names followed by a printer statement in W2119 only

conclusions: Both separately catalogued 1529 Zürich prints W2118 and W2119 visibly contain the key shared Eucharistic statements, the Mass-as-not-meritorious-work clause, and nonagreement concerning bodily presence in Article 15.
The three additions described by Zürich archivists at Arts 7, 13, 15 are present as propositions in both these prints (without proving original Z autograph identity).
W2119 photographed signatory page includes the Zürich / Christoph Froschauer printer colophon; W2118 corresponding page lists signatories but does not include that printer statement beneath them.
A difference in printed colophon is a bibliographical difference, NOT in itself evidence of a separately typeset body, priority of issue, direct copying, or which manuscript underlies each edition.
W2119 physical copy has extensive handwritten Latin annotations; these are later/owner marginal notes of undetermined author/date and not a variant in 1529 printed text.
W2118 institutional PDF now accessible via stable catalog ID 291747, resolving V4.64 access limitation. Original 1529 print is seen; original signed Z and K manuscript pages remain unread.
